item.title: UNC chancellor on Bill Belichick: "Support comes with expectations"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Internal turmoil at the North Carolina football program brought down G.M.
item.content:encoded:
Internal turmoil at the North Carolina football program brought down G.M. Michael Lombardi and defensive coordinator Steve Belichick. Head coach Bill Belichick remains.

Earlier this week UNC chancellor Lee Roberts addressed the investigation that prompted the resignation of Bill Belichick's consigliere and his son.

"Coach Belichick continues to have our support, the support of the administration and of the board [of trustees]," Roberts said Thursday, via Brad Crawford of CBS Sports. "He understands that that support comes with expectations around conduct and behavior. Nobody understands that better than coach Belichick."

As to Lombardi and Steve Belichick, the conduct and behavior apparently fell short of the standard. Given their proximity to the head coach, that's problematic.

"We're continuing to put in place policies and training and monitoring to make sure that the standards we expect of the football program are being adhered to," Roberts said.

The message is clear. The powers-that-be have their eyes on Bill Belichick. And if they can pin something/anything to him, they can escape the Belichick experiment without owing him a buyout.

North Carolina is off this weekend. The 2-1 Tar Heels host Notre Dame next weekend.

item.title: Deion Sanders on Travis Hunter's usage: "I have no idea what's going on"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Back in May, Colorado coach Deion Sanders expressed disappointment that he hadn't heard from the Jaguars regarding how to coach, and how to deploy, cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter.
item.content:encoded:
Back in May, Colorado coach Deion Sanders expressed disappointment that he hadn’t heard from the Jaguars regarding how to coach, and how to deploy, cornerback/receiver Travis Hunter. Two games into Hunter's second NFL season, Coach Prime remains perplexed about Hunter's workload.

"I don't ask questions because I'm not there," Sanders said recently on his CBS Colorado show. "I don't know what transpires when we're not looking. I have no idea what’s going on. I know who he was and who he is right now. I know what he's capable of. I do know that."

In Week 1, Hunter got four snaps on offense and 29 on defense. He had one catch for eight yards.

In Week 2, Hunter had six snaps on offense and 37 on defense. He wasn't targeted in the Jacksonville passing game.

The lack of usage for a player who entered the league with the promise of being the first true full-time two-way player since Chuck Bednarik has sparked plenty of questions. Earlier this week, coach Liam Coen said the team will be looking at giving him more reps this week, on both sides of the ball.

Asked on Friday whether Hunter has spoken to coaches about the rotation at cornerback this week, Hunter opted for discretion.

"I'm gonna leave that up to the coaches to answer," Hunter said. "That ain’t for me to answer."

In an appearance on The Pivot podcast before the start of the regular season, Hunter reiterated his belief that he can reach his full potential as a cornerback and as a receiver.

Ryan Clark told Hunter that he could be a Hall of Fame cornerback or a Pro Bowl-caliber receiver. But Clark's implicit message was clear — it's impossible to be both. How can Hunter accomplish it?

"Work ethic," Hunter said. "We all get the same 24 hours."

Channing Crowder pressed Hunter on his effort to use that 24 hours to do both at the highest possible level. "The numbers don't work out," Crowder said.

"If I'm trying to be the best — how are you gonna be the best, if you ain't trying to be the best? If you ain't trying to compete and do the best to be the best? So my main focus is be the best. So I'm gonna do everything I can do to be the best. I don't want to be the best at one position. There's a lot of people that's the best at one position. Ain't nobody yet been the best at both, full-time."

For now, Hunter has played on a part-time basis on defense, with cameo appearances on offense. What's his preference?

"I like doing both," Hunter said. "And I cannot sit on the sideline. I don't think nobody's noticed that yet. I hate the sidelines. I do not wanna sit there. I can't sit there and just watch football. I've got to be on the field."

Clark pointed out that 52 other guys spend time on the sidelines. "That's their problem," Hunter said.

He was smiling when he said it, but there's no escaping his point. Hunter still wants to play on a full-time basis on both sides of the ball. But he's playing so little on each side of the ball that the snaps don't add up to the amount of time he'd be getting if he played all snaps on offense or all snaps on defense.

It's still not clear what the Jaguars are doing with the player whom they moved up from No. 5 to No. 2 in the draft to get, with the justification that they'd be getting two players in one. At some point, the idea of a two-way player has yielded to the reality that, as Crowder said, the numbers don't work out. It's too hard to be fully and completely prepared to perform at a high level on both offense and defense.

And it's almost as if the Jaguars want Hunter to come to the conclusion on his own that he'll accept playing one side of the ball or the other in order to get a full-time workload at one speciic position.

Still, if the Jaguars weren't prepared to let Hunter do what he clearly wants to do (and he surely made his point clear to them before the draft), why did they give up so much to make him the second overall pick in the draft?

That's the most confounding aspect of this. Everyone knew Hunter wanted to play both ways. The decision to trade up to get Hunter sent a message that the Jaguars were on board with that approach. The numbers, to date, paint a far different picture.

item.title: Titans-Giants tickets are available for as little as $17
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Two months ago, the price point for a ticket for a specific event at MetLife Stadium landed as high as $39,704.
item.content:encoded:
Two months ago, the price point for a ticket for a specific event at MetLife Stadium landed as high as $39,704. On Sunday, it will be considerably cheaper to get in to the building.

At TickPick, the get-in price for Titans-Giants is as low as $17. At Ticketmaster, the league's official reselling partner (by the way, it's amazing how many previously seedy and illegal businesses became respectable and legitimate once corporate America figured out how to profit from them), there are plenty of tickets at $20 or $21.

There are good reasons for the football game to be viewed as far less desirable to attend than the World Cup Final. First, the Giants have lost their starting quarterback for the season. (Yes, Jaxson Dart supposedly could return for the postseason. But if they manage to get that far without him, why bring him back when he hasn't played in months?) Second, the Titans aren't exactly a road draw. Third, and perhaps most importantly, it's a bad weather weekend in New Jersey, thanks to a nor'easter that will bring plenty of rain and wind to the region.

But if you're willing to brave the elements and you're willing to answer Cam Skattebo’s call and you've got a portrait of Andrew Jackson burning a hole in your pocket, you can go to the game.

item.title: Seven teams face an 0-3 hole — and only seven 0-3 teams have ever made the playoffs
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Eight teams entered Week 3 at 0-2.
item.content:encoded:
Eight teams entered Week 3 at 0-2. One of them — the Falcons — avoided an 0-3 start. For the others, it becomes imperative to avoid starting the year with three straight losses.

In NFL history, only seven teams have made the playoffs after starting 0-3. The group includes the 2025 Texans, the 2018 Texans, the 1998 Bills, the 1995 Lions, the 1992 Chargers, the 1982 Buccaneers, and the 1981 Jets.

Only the '92 Chargers made it to the postseason after starting 0-4.

It's easier now than it once was, thanks to 17 regular-season games and seven playoff spots per conference. It's still not easy.

For starters, plenty of teams that start 0-3 do so for a very good reason — they're not very good. Those that are have a reduced margin for error over the final 14 games.

This year, one game features two 0-2 teams: the Texans at the Colts. The other winless teams are the Dolphins, the Titans, the Chargers, the Commanders, and the Buccaneers.

item.title: Brian Daboll downplays revenge as motivation for Titans-Giants game
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll will be coaching against the team that fired him when he faces the Giants on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll will be coaching against the team that fired him when he faces the Giants on Sunday. He says that's not particularly important.

Daboll, who was hired as Giants head coach in 2022 and fired last year, said he can set aside any emotions associated with facing his former team and just focus on doing his job.

"I've faced a lot of former teams before," Daboll said. "It's a one-week season every week, so you've got to put everything you got into it. You've got to get ready for scheme, new coordinators on their end, different players. As simple as it sounds, that's what it is every week in the National Football League. I have a ton of respect for the people in that organization. Very grateful for the opportunity the Mara family and Tisch family gave me. From top down to the bottom, really good people in that building. But it's about getting the players ready for a game. I've been on a number of teams that played my former teams before. But the focus is on our players."

Daboll also downplayed any idea that he has an advantage because he knows the players on the Giants, noting that they're a different team this year than they were last year. Daboll is treating Sunday like he'd treat any other game.

item.title: Commanders announce Marcus Mariota will be a team captain for the rest of the season
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Mariota will start in place of the injured Jayden Daniels on Sunday against the Seahawks.
item.content:encoded:
Marcus Mariota will be the Commanders' starting quarterback for whatever games Jayden Daniels misses with his left elbow injury. And Mariota and Daniels will both be team captains for the rest of the season.

Commanders coach Dan Quinn announced on Friday that the five Commanders who were chosen as team captains before the season got together and decided they want Mariota to be a captain, not just while he's the starting quarterback but also when he returns to the No. 2 job when Daniels returns.

"I thought it was such a cool thing: The captains huddled up with me earlier in week and said, 'We'd like to make Marcus our sixth captain,'" Quinn said. "I thought, What a great tribute of brotherhood of those guys asking. They were all as on board as you could imagine. I thought it was awesome, too. What a great example of teammate and leadership."

The Commanders say Mariota's status as captain for the rest of the season is not an indication that he'll be starting for long, as the team expects Daniels to be back soon. But even if Mariota spends most of the season on the bench, he'll have the captain's C on his jersey.

In addition to Mariota and Daniels, the Commanders' captains are wide receiver Terry McLaurin, linebacker Frankie Luvu, safety Jeremy Reaves and punter Tress Way.

item.title: After Week 2 stinger, Saquon Barkley vows to be "fearless"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Barkley missed much of Sunday's game after injury.
item.content:encoded:
A stinger grossly shortened Eagles running back Saquon Barkley's day against the Titans in Week 2. As a Week 3 Monday night game against the Bears looms, Barkley is undeterred — but also cognizant of the situation.

"I’ve had a history of [stingers] before," Barkley said Friday, via Tim McManus of ESPN. "This is the first bad one I had in a long time. It's also like a wake-up call to me. I've been super active focusing on my lower body and longevity of my career. I probably wasn't as great as I needed to be with my neck stability and strengthening my neck. So it's putting that within my routine and having that as part of my process and kind of the same way I attack everything from head to toe, do the same thing with my neck.

"It's good to have an MRI knowing it's nothing, hopefully, God willing, where I worry about my career and I can just go out there and play free."

The injury happened on the first play from scrimmage at Tennessee. Barkley later returned wearing a neck collar, but he finished the day with only four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards.

Barkley was limited in practice on Thursday. He fully participated on Friday.

Will the injury affect him on Monday?

"I don't think so," Barkley said. "That's why I'm rehabbing my ass off, to get it as strong as it needs to be. I feel like I'm in a really good spot. I know they wouldn't let me go out there if I wasn't able to do it.

"I'm going to let the game come, and I'm going to go out there and play fearless, don't worry about."

The Eagles are 2-0 after narrow wins against the overmatched Commanders and Titans. Philly may be facing a third-string quarterback in Chicago on Monday night, giving the Eagles a golden opportunity to move to 3-0.

item.title: Tim Tebow pauses his relationship with Life Surge after Pablo Torre investigation
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Pablo Torre is a troublemaker.
item.content:encoded:
Pablo Torre is a troublemaker. In the best way possible.

A recent episode of Pablo Torre Finds Out explored the entity known as Life Surge, which allegedly has preyed on Christians who attend events featuring speakers like former NFL quarterback Tim Tebow in an effort to get them to plunk down cash to sign up for classes on how to make money.

It was enough to get Tebow to suspend his dealings with Life Surge.

“The allegations are extremely, extremely serious,” Tebow told reporters on Friday, "and it’s something that we take very serious. And so for us, we’re having our team do an investigation but also pausing our relationship 'til we can learn more about the facts to be able to understand more.”

Tebow was asked whether he knew about the situation before Torre's investigation.

“Honestly, I was at a anti-human trafficking conference yesterday, and the team shared with me when we were leaving as we were flying to Alabama for [an] event,” Tebow said. “And kind of caught off guard with some of it, and I think that’s why we’re trying to understand more of the facts to really learn it.”

That's hardly a clear and unequivocal denial. Regardless, Torre's investigation put just enough of a spotlight on the situation to get Tebow to back away, regardless of what he knew or should have known before Torre pulled the curtain back on Life Surge.

It's possible the group duped Tebow in the same way it allegedly duped those who attended the events at which Tebow spoke. Historically, plenty of Christians have had their strong beliefs leveraged into plenty of money for charlatans who regard intense faith as an opportunity to make easy money.

item.title: Bud Light leans in to fines for beer celebrations
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Church Lady has commandeered the league office.
item.content:encoded:
The Church Lady has commandeered the league office. And the league's official beer sponsor has taken full advantage of it.

Three different fines issued were this week to players who mimed the consumption of a beverage that the NFL presumed to be beer. Bud Light, which reportedly pays the NFL $250 million per year, has leaned in to the league's crackdown.

Tweeted the Bud Light official account: "$37,384 in the jar … how many beers will that buy for everybody this weekend?"

That highly-specific amount represents the exact sum of the fines imposed on 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk ($14,926), Colts guard Matt Goncalves ($8,847), and Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson ($13,611).

Meanwhile, and as Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News notes, the Cowboys have Miller Lite logos all over the backdrop for their press conferences in Brazil, where they'll be playing the Ravens this weekend.

It's all ridiculously hypocritical for the NFL. But the league doesn't care.

For the NFL, it's do as we say, not as we brew.

item.title: Bears ST coach says Eagles are violating intent of the rule by using holder on kickoffs
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Last week, the Eagles used a holder on their kickoffs so that the ball could be placed at an angle that affected the trajectory of the ball and made it harder for the returner to field.
item.content:encoded:
Last week, the Eagles used a holder on their kickoffs so that the ball could be placed at an angle that affected the trajectory of the ball and made it harder for the returner to field. This week, the Bears are preparing to face the Eagles on Monday night, and Bears special teams coordinator Richard Hightower says he doesn't think the Eagles should be able to do that.

Hightower, who was one of the special teams coaches who was involved in adopting the NFL's "dynamic" kickoff, said permitting a 12th player on the field to hold the ball was intended to be for windy conditions with the ball in a tee, and not for what the Eagles are doing.

"Two years we talked about it, where you could use a holder," Hightower said. "It evolved to weather-related only. This past year it changed to you can use it at any time. But . . . the intent of the rule is the ball is supposed to be in a tee when you have a holder out there. It's not to be used like you've seen it used here lately."

Hightower said there was a conference call with special teams coaches scheduled to discuss the matter.

"We're all getting together on that shortly and we hope to get that fixed and corrected within the language of everything done in the rulebook," Hightower said.

Hightower said he believes the NFL could make a change now requiring that the ball is placed in a tee if there's a holder on a kickoff, and that the change wouldn't need to wait until the offseason.

"That's the intent of the rule and what we want to have happen, so that's the way it should be, and that's the way we'd like it going forward," Hightower said.

There's precedent for the NFL making such a change during the season: In 2022, the Raiders were using a holder on kickoffs to place the ball on top of the tee, rather than in the tee, something the NFL initially allowed — only to change course during the season and ban it. Hightower wants to see the NFL do the same thing with the Eagles' tactic.

item.title: Josh Allen is having a historic start to the season
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Bills quarterback Josh Allen has gotten off to a great start in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
Bills quarterback Josh Allen has gotten off to a great start in 2026. He's already made a little history — and he could make some more.

Per NBC Sports research, Allen is one of only three players with nine or more total touchdowns and no turnovers in the first two games of the season. The others — Patrick Mahomes in 2018 and Peyton Manning in 2013 — won the NFL MVP award that same year.

With at least two touchdowns and no turnovers against the Chargers on Sunday, Allen would join Mahomes as the only players with 11 or more touchdowns and no turnovers through three games. (Mahomes had 13 touchdowns and no turnovers through three games in 2018.)

And there's more. Allen has had two straight games with four or more touchdowns and no interceptions. If he does it again on Sunday, he'll tie five players for the longest streak in league history: Matthew Stafford in 2025, Allen in 2024, Lamar Jackson in 2019, Drew Brees in 2018, and Russell Wilson in 2015.

Finally, Allen has had two straight games with two rushing touchdowns. Only three players have done that in the first three games of the season: Priest Holmes in 2003, Stephen Davis in 1999, and Jim Brown in 1958.

Allen would trade it all for a 3-0 start, for the third straight season. And to extend Buffalo's home record to 19-2 over the past 21 games.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan on Nick Bosa's injury: I know he's bummed, but he'll be back
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed defensive end Nick Bosa will miss multiple weeks after injuring his calf before Thursday's practice.
item.content:encoded:
49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed defensive end Nick Bosa will miss multiple weeks after injuring his calf before Thursday's practice.

"We can't say exactly, but I'm guessing around a few weeks," Shanahan said of Bosa's timeline, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com.

The 49ers ruled out Bosa and rookie defensive end Romello Height (hand surgery) for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. They have been hit hard by injuries in the defensive line.

Defensive tackle C.J. West (knee), defensive end Sam Okuayinonu (foot) and defensive tackle Alfred Collins (patellar tendon) are on injured reserve. Rookie defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. has a high-ankle sprain that will keep him out multiple weeks.

"Losing Bosa was rough yesterday," Shanahan said. "I mean, losing six out of the 10 D-linemen in the last two weeks that have made our team is a little unusual. I don't think I've been a part of that, so that has been different."

Bosa returned from a torn ACL in his right knee and played 70 snaps over the first two games. He injured his knee in Week 3 last season, almost exactly a year ago, in a game against the Cardinals.

It is unclear whether Bosa injured his right calf, as Shanahan said he wasn't sure.

Bosa was warming up before the walkthrough when he injured his calf.

"I know he's bummed out, but he'll be back," Shanahan said.

The 49ers are still deciding whether to place Bosa on injured reserve. Only eight players can return from IR during the season, and the team already has several players on IR who it plans to return to the roster.

"He's right there at that point, along with a couple of other guys that are all in the same boat," Shanahan said. "Because of the number we have on [injured reserve], we won't be able to do all of them. So we've got to decide, and we're just trying to guess which ones will go longer, which ones have the chances of being sooner, and it's just a guess.

"They're all really in the same boat, so we've got to decide that by tomorrow."

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said that he expects to be good to go for Monday night's game against the Bears and Friday's injury report shows that he's on track to play.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said that he expects to be good to go for Monday night's game against the Bears and Friday's injury report shows that he's on track to play.

Barkley was up to full participation after getting in a limited session on Thursday. Barkley suffered a stinger in last Sunday's win over the Titans.

Wide receiver Hollywood Brown (ankle) was added to the injury report on Friday and he did not practice. Tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) remained out of practice.

Running back Tank Bigsby (abdomen), running back Will Shipley (foot), and wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were limited after missing Thursday's practice. Linebacker Jonathan Greenard (pectoral) was also limited while defensive tackle Jalen Carter (wrist), safety Andrew Mukuba (knee), and guard Tyler Steen (shoulder) were full participants.

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans is questionable with a hip injury
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans returned to practice Friday, but he is questionable to play Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
49ers wide receiver Mike Evans returned to practice Friday, but he is questionable to play Sunday.

Evans' hip injury kept him out of practice on Wednesday and Thursday.

He has nine catches for 103 yards and a touchdown in two games.

Evans missed nine games in 2025 and three games the previous season after sitting out only nine games over his first 10 seasons.

The 49ers ruled out defensive end Nick Bosa (knee/calf), defensive end Romello Height (hand), wide receiver Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and defensive tackle James Thompson (ankle).

Bosa injured a calf muscle during Thursday's practice, and he is expected to miss multiple weeks.

Height underwent hand surgery this week, and Robinson and Thompson have high-ankle sprains that could keep them out multiple weeks.

item.content:encoded:
The Bills have signed wide receiver Greg Dortch to the active roster from the practice squad, the team announced Friday.

In a corresponding move, the Bills placed defensive back Jordan Hancock on injured reserve.

Hancock missed Thursday and Friday's practice due to a hamstring injury.

He played 13 defensive snaps and 42 on special teams in the first two games and totaled five tackles.

The Bills elevated Dortch for the first two games. He returned five punts for 46 yards (9.2 avg.) and five kicks for 133 (26.6 avg).

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Titans running back Tony Pollard (ankle) had a second consecutive limited practice Friday after missing Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Titans running back Tony Pollard (ankle) had a second consecutive limited practice Friday after missing Wednesday. Pollard, though, did not receive an injury designation for Sunday.

That is good news for the Titans because running back Tyjae Spears (ankle) is questionable to play. Spears returned to practice Friday on a limited basis.

Rookie running back Nick Singleton made his regular-season debut in Week 2 and could see more work this week because of Pollard and Spears' injuries.

"He’s doing a really good job," Titans coach Robert Saleh said Friday, via Jim Wyatt of the team website. "He's probably 50-50 on the read [on his runs], but to be expected from a young buck. So, hopefully we get him a couple more. But overall I think he's going to be a good back, he's going in the right direction."

Singleton, selected in the fifth round out of Penn State, carried the ball four times for 10 yards against the Eagles.

The Titans also list cornerback Cor'Dale Flott (quad) as questionable after he had three limited practices this week.

item.title: JC Tretter: Field condition in Brazil "reinforces" NFLPA concerns about international games
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Sunday's game between the Ravens and Cowboys in Brazil will be played on a grass field that likely will not look great on TV.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday's game between the Ravens and Cowboys in Brazil will be played on a grass field that likely will not look great on TV. It also will present challenges for the players, especially when it comes to wearing the right cleats.

NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter has weighed in on the issue. And he has pointed to the obvious red flag regarding the general field quality at stadiums that rarely host NFL games.

"There have been a lot of questions about the field surface in Brazil, and I wanted to provide the NFLPA’s perspective," Tretter said in a lengthy message posted on Twitter.

"Our number one priority is the health and safety of our players. The concern heading into this week was that the field would be loose, patchy, and lead to excessive slipping. Those conditions are generally more of a playability and performance issue than a significant injury concern.

"But safety isn't the only standard. Players should be able to perform at the level they expect of themselves and that fans expect from them. A thin, slick field may not present the same risks as a surface with too much traction, but it still affects performance and the quality of the game.

"We've been in regular communication with the league about the field. Both the NFLPA's and the league's field experts have been on the ground in Brazil for days, monitoring conditions and working to make the surface as safe and playable as possible for Sunday.

"Based on our experts' assessment, the field needed better traction and stability. They recommended reinforced stitching to help the surface hold together and brought in equipment to reinforce as much of the field as possible before the game. Our experts will remain engaged and continue evaluating conditions through kickoff.

"The work happening this week also highlights two larger issues.

"First, we need field standards that account for both safety and performance. The NFL, NFLPA, and our field and engineering experts spend a lot of time working on these issues, and we've made progress. But we're not where we need to be yet. We can't have surfaces that melt players' cleats, like we saw in Nashville last week. We can't have frozen fields that create unnecessary risks. The best athletes in the world should be playing on surfaces that meet the same standard of excellence we expect from them every week.

"Second, this reinforces one of our concerns about international expansion. Two of the three games played in Brazil have had field-related issues. That's not a coincidence. This time of year makes it extremely challenging to maintain the kind of grass surface we expect at the NFL level.

"Our guys are exceptional at what they do, and I'm confident they'll put on a terrific game in Rio this week. They always do. But we owe it to them to provide the best possible opportunity to succeed. Players can overcome a lot. But they shouldn't have to overcome the field.

"The NFL has been clear they want to continue to grow the game internationally. However, growth alone cannot be the goal. The goal has to be growing the game while maintaining the standards our players deserve. If we can't do both, then we need to make different decisions."

The problem is that the NFL has already made the decision to expand the slate of international games from 10 per year to 16. As to field quality, it would be better to have a team or two based in other countries, since that would give the league a reason to ensure that the field will be good enough for all 10 home games played there.

For now, the league intends to, in theory, have every team play one international game per year. And while the NFLPA isn't required to agree to that term in the next Collective Bargaining Agreement, the league will surely lock out the players until they agree to both 18 regular-season games and 16 annual international games.

The best the players can do is negotiate the best concessions in exchange. Field quality shouldn't be a concession. The league's desire to save money and to expand revenue potential for non-football events has contributed to the current number of artificial fields. The issue is different as to international games; cities need to be selected with the quality of the games to be played there as one of the top priorities.

In Brazil, it clearly is not.

item.content:encoded:
The Browns may be without two of their key defensive starters for their 2026 home opener against the Panthers.

Cleveland has listed cornerback Tyson Campbell and safety Grant Delpit as questionable for Week 3.

Campbell had been limited on Wednesday and Thursday with an ankle injury. The team added a knee injury to the report on Friday, with Campbell again a limited participant.

Delpit was limited all week with a shoulder injury.

“They went through practice today and we'll see where they're at," Monken said Friday, via Kelsey Russo of the team’s website. "They [did] a little work here post-practice, but we're hopeful they'll be able to go.”

Additionally, the Browns ruled out guard Teven Jenkins with a back injury. He did not practice this week.
